articles.blogTitle: Auto Parts From China: Fitment and Sourcing Checks
articles.blogContent:
Auto accessories and spare parts can be profitable in Nigeria because vehicle owners constantly need replacements, upgrades and practical add-ons. But this category requires discipline. Wrong fitment, weak material, fake specifications or unsafe components can create returns, complaints and real safety problems.

This guide is most suitable for accessories and selected non-critical parts. For safety-critical components, buyers need stronger technical knowledge, supplier verification and compliance checks. Do not treat brake, steering, electrical safety or structural components as casual imports.

Fitment is the first risk

A car accessory can look correct and still fail because it does not fit the Nigerian vehicle models customers own. Confirm model, year, trim, left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive relevance, connector type and size. Do not buy based only on a product title.

Keep photos, measurements and compatibility notes in your buying file. For repeat sellers, create SKUs tied to exact vehicle applications so future reorders do not depend on memory.

Quality matters more than cheap price

Auto buyers may tolerate low prices, but they do not tolerate parts that fail quickly. Ask suppliers for material details, product videos, packaging and previous supply evidence. A supplier specializing in one category is often safer than a random store with thousands of unrelated items.

Use the supplier verification checklist and quote comparison guide before choosing. If the item is technical or high risk, use Corporate Sourcing.

Shipping weight and damage risk matter

Some auto accessories are bulky or fragile. Ask for carton dimensions and gross weight before payment. Poor packaging can cause breakage, scratches or missing parts. Include packaging quality in the supplier decision.

Use the CBM Calculator and Landed Cost Estimator before approving the order. A heavy product with weak margin may not be worth importing.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Confirm vehicle model, year range and fitment details.
  • Avoid safety-critical parts without technical verification.
  • Request material, warranty and product proof.
  • Compare supplier specialization, not only price.
  • Calculate landed cost after weight and carton data.
  • Test market demand before scaling quantities.

Build a fitment record that another person can use

Record the vehicle make, model, production year, engine or body variant where relevant, exact part number and any superseded numbers. Include connector photographs and dimensions. Use a qualified parts specialist to resolve compatibility rather than assuming a broad year range in a marketplace title is correct. Vehicles sold under the same name in different markets may use different components.

If a customer supplies a VIN or other vehicle information, use it only for the necessary fitment check and handle it appropriately. Do not post customer identifiers in public listings or supplier groups. Ask the supplier to confirm the exact application in writing and retain that response with the order.

Keep safety-critical parts outside casual trial buying

Brake, steering, restraint and other safety-critical components need competent technical evaluation, traceability and the relevant conformity evidence. A low failure rate claimed by a seller is not enough. Do not test an unverified safety component on a customer's vehicle. Establish the applicable requirements with the relevant authorities and qualified professionals before purchasing.

CheckWhat to record
IdentityManufacturer, exact model or part number and batch markings
CompatibilityConfirmed vehicle application and any exclusions
Authenticity claimEvidence supporting any genuine-brand or authorised-supply statement
ConditionNew, used, remanufactured or refurbished, clearly defined
RemedyHow wrong fitment, defects and transit damage will be handled

Compare a kit with its complete bill of materials

A trim or mounting kit may need clips, brackets, fasteners and instructions. Ask for an itemised list and photographs of everything supplied. An apparently cheaper kit can require expensive local improvisation. Do not substitute fasteners or mounting methods where doing so could compromise safe installation; have the responsible technician assess the requirements.

Price returns into the decision

Suppose 100 non-critical accessories cost ₦500,000 delivered and 10 cannot be sold because of wrong fitment. The purchase cost per saleable unit becomes about ₦5,556 before selling costs. If correcting the compatibility file prevents those errors, the improvement may be worth more than a small supplier discount. This is an illustrative calculation, not an expected defect rate.

Keep returns by reason: wrong catalogue application, buyer selection error, manufacturing defect or shipping damage. Each requires a different correction. Reordering the same part without resolving the cause repeats the loss. Check import restrictions for the exact category and condition before paying, especially where used parts or other restricted goods are involved.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: Construction Hardware From China: Procurement for Nigeria
articles.blogContent:
Construction and hardware sourcing from China can support Nigerian projects, contractors, developers and facilities teams, but it is not a category for vague buying. Measurements, material grade, standards, durability, installation requirements and delivery timing matter. A wrong specification can delay a project or create rework.

This guide is for selected supplies, fittings, tools, hardware, fixtures and project-related items where the buyer can define requirements clearly. For technical or regulated building materials, involve qualified professionals and check compliance before purchase.

Start from project specification

A project buyer should not ask suppliers for generic items. Define dimensions, material, finish, load requirement, colour, installation environment, quantity and acceptable tolerance. If the item must match an existing design or technical standard, state that clearly.

For business orders, use Corporate Sourcing so supplier communication, comparison and documentation are handled properly. Project procurement needs a stronger record than casual shopping.

Samples and proof can prevent rework

For visible finishes, fittings, fixtures, tools or hardware that affects installation, samples or production proof may be worth the cost. A wrong finish or weak material can create project delays that cost more than inspection.

Use Product Samples From China to Nigeria and the import documentation checklist before approving bulk purchase. Written approval protects the project owner and procurement team.

Shipping and handling must match the product

Construction and hardware supplies can be heavy, sharp, fragile or awkwardly shaped. Ask for packing method, gross weight, carton dimensions and whether pallets or crates are needed. Poor packing can damage goods before they reach site.

Use the CBM Calculator and compare routes with Air vs Sea Calculator. Most project supplies need timeline planning, not last-minute air freight panic.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Project specification approved before supplier search.
  • Measurements, material grade and finish defined.
  • Supplier proof and samples requested where risk is high.
  • Carton, pallet or crate data checked before shipping.
  • Timeline aligned with project schedule.
  • Compliance and professional suitability confirmed before payment.

Turn the design into an approved procurement schedule

Use the project drawing or bill of quantities as the starting point. For each item, record its drawing reference, material grade, dimensions, finish, quantity, installation location and applicable performance requirement. Assign a revision number. A supplier should quote against that revision, and the project professional should approve any proposed substitution before production.

Do not allow a supplier's “equivalent” description to replace engineering review. Structural fixings, electrical components, fire-related products and other safety-critical materials need evidence appropriate to their intended use. A visually similar sample cannot establish load capacity, fire performance or electrical safety.

Check the interfaces that cause installation failures

InterfaceQuestion for the project team
Door hardwareDoes it match door thickness, handing, frame preparation and the specified function?
Plumbing fittingAre connection type, dimensions and intended operating conditions confirmed?
Visible finishHas the actual sample been approved beside adjacent materials?
Equipment mountingHas a competent professional approved the mounting method and substrate?
Replacement componentDoes the exact reference match the installed system?

Order to the installation sequence

A building programme may need concealed fittings before finishes and replacement spares only at handover. Divide the purchasing schedule accordingly. Ask the site manager for the date each item must be accepted on site, then work backwards through procurement, inspection, transport and clearance. An early arrival can also be costly if the site lacks secure, dry storage.

For example, if 80 rooms each require four approved handles, the base requirement is 320. Any spares should be a deliberate allowance approved by the project team. Keep left/right versions, special rooms and inaccessible replacements separate. Do not add a flat percentage to every line without checking whether the items are interchangeable.

Make packaging serve the site

Request labels by building, floor or installation zone where practical. Keep matching finish batches identifiable. Include the lifting and unloading plan for heavy crates in the destination cost comparison. A shipment that fits in a container may still require equipment to move safely from the vehicle to the storage area.

Close out with records, not just delivery receipts

At receipt, reconcile quantities and condition against the approved schedule. Keep certificates, drawings, instructions and spare-part information for the facilities team. Delivery acceptance should not silently substitute for technical acceptance. Escalate deviations before installation, because removing an unsuitable fitting after finishes are complete can cost far more than the original item.

Check SON's import conformity guidance and the current Customs classification for the exact goods. A project description such as “hardware” is too broad to establish requirements or a duty rate.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • Nigerian import prohibition reference
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: Furniture Sourcing for Nigeria: Import Checks and Costs
articles.blogContent:
Resolve import eligibility before comparing furniture prices

Do not assume that all furniture can be imported into Nigeria. The FCCPC's published prohibition reference includes furniture categories, while the trade portal's displayed list differs. These public summaries are not a reliable basis for treating an unlisted item as automatically permitted. Obtain current written clarification for the exact HS classification, material, condition and intended use before committing money.

Ask the clearing professional to identify the current rule and any claimed exception, then verify it with the relevant authority. A supplier's ability to ship, or another importer's past delivery, is not proof of eligibility. If the proposed route is prohibited, compare Nigerian manufacturing or local supply. The cost and packing methods below apply only after the proposed purchase is confirmed lawful.

Furniture can look profitable until shipping and damage risk are included. Chairs, tables, shelves, sofas, salon furniture, office furniture and hospitality furniture are often bulky. A low supplier price can become expensive when CBM, packaging, clearing and local delivery are added.

For offices, hotels, restaurants, shortlets and other projects, establish import eligibility first. Then compare specifications, packing, installation and lawful local alternatives.

Furniture must be specified physically

Photos are not enough. Ask for dimensions, material, frame, finish, foam density where relevant, fabric or leather type, load capacity, assembly method and packing style. If the product is for a business space, confirm whether it matches the use case.

For hotels, offices and restaurants, read the hospitality and office sourcing guides in our buying guides. Use Corporate Sourcing when the order supports a project, team or physical space.

CBM decides whether the deal works

Furniture is usually a volume problem. A chair may not be heavy, but it can occupy space. Ask for packed dimensions, not only product dimensions. Knock-down or flat-pack furniture may ship better than fully assembled pieces.

Use the CBM Calculator before payment. If the CBM makes the landed cost too high, renegotiate packaging, choose another model or consider local alternatives.

Plan around damage and timeline

Furniture can scratch, dent, break or stain in transit. Packaging should protect corners, surfaces, legs and fragile parts. Ask for packaging photos and carton/crate details. For large orders, sea freight usually makes more sense than air, but it requires time.

Use Sea Shipping From China to Nigeria and Ship With Us once goods are ready. Build local delivery and handling into landed cost because furniture does not end at the port or warehouse.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Dimensions, material, finish and assembly requirement confirmed.
  • Supplier photos, videos or samples reviewed.
  • Packaging method and damage protection checked.
  • CBM calculated before payment.
  • Sea shipping timeline planned where appropriate.
  • Local delivery and installation costs included in landed cost.

Compare usable installed cost

Include the product, approved protective packing, freight, applicable destination charges, local vehicle, unloading, assembly and disposal of packaging. Check access through doors, staircases and lifts. A sofa that fits the room can still be impossible to move through the building without costly changes.

MeasurementWhy it matters
Assembled dimensionsFit and circulation in the intended space
Largest packed componentAccess through delivery routes
Carton dimensions and quantityShipping volume and warehouse space
Gross weightHandling and unloading requirements
Assembly detailsLabour, tools, missing-part risk and final acceptance

Model the packing choice

As an arithmetic example, an assembled item packed in 0.50 cubic metres uses 10 cubic metres for 20 units. An approved flat-pack version occupying 0.18 cubic metres per unit uses 3.6 cubic metres. The difference is 6.4 cubic metres, but the flat-pack choice may add assembly labour and hardware checks. Ask the forwarder to quote both actual packing plans; do not multiply by an unverified rate and treat it as a firm saving.

Agree how damage and missing parts will be handled

Specify corner protection, surface separation, moisture protection appropriate to the materials and identification of assembly hardware. Request packing photographs before dispatch. At delivery, photograph damage before discarding wrapping and reconcile every package against the packing list. Keep matching finish or fabric references because an unmatched replacement part may be commercially unusable.

For project furniture, approve a representative sample or prototype against the intended use before ordering a room's worth. Confirm that the design, durability evidence and maintenance requirements suit the setting. A domestic-use product is not automatically suitable for a hotel or public waiting area. Keep the final decision tied to lawful eligibility, usable installed cost and the accepted specification.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: China Import Cash Flow: A Planning Guide for Nigerian SMEs
articles.blogContent:
Import profit is not only about margin. It is also about cash flow. A Nigerian SME can buy a profitable product and still struggle if too much money is tied down in supplier payment, slow shipping, Customs, unsold stock or customer credit. Cash-flow discipline decides whether importation strengthens or weakens the business.

This guide builds on How To Build a China Import Budget and How Nigerian Wholesalers Can Build Repeat Supply Lines From China. It is for SMEs that need import decisions to support working capital, not swallow it.

Order size should follow sales evidence

Large orders can reduce unit cost, but they also tie down cash. If the product is untested, a smaller order may protect the business. If demand is proven, larger orders may make sense because the sales cycle is clearer.

Do not let supplier discounts override your cash position. A discount that produces slow stock can be worse than a higher unit cost on a faster-moving quantity.

Shipping speed affects cash recovery

Air freight costs more but may allow faster sales and faster cash recovery. Sea freight costs less but keeps money tied down longer. The better route depends on margin, urgency, product volume and working capital.

Use Air vs Sea Calculator with the Landed Cost Estimator. The cheapest route is not always the best cash-flow route.

Keep a reserve, not just a purchase budget

Exchange movement, local delivery, damages, slow stock and marketing costs can all appear after payment. A business that has no reserve may be forced to borrow, discount too early or delay the next order.

Use a Sure Imports account to keep import requests organized and use Pay Supplier only after the full cash requirement is clear.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Do not commit all cash to supplier payment.
  • Match order size to realistic sales speed.
  • Compare air and sea against cash-flow timing.
  • Keep reserve for exchange, delivery and slow sales.
  • Track actual landed cost after every order.
  • Reorder based on stock movement, not supplier pressure.

Plot the cash dates before calculating the margin

Create a weekly schedule showing opening cash, supplier payments, logistics payments, operating expenses and customer receipts. Use the date money is expected to leave or reach the bank. An invoice issued to a customer is not cash received, and an estimated profit is not money available to pay the freight bill.

Illustrative milestoneCash outflowCash remaining from ₦2 million
Supplier deposit₦400,000₦1,600,000
Supplier balance₦600,000₦1,000,000
Logistics and destination costs₦450,000₦550,000
Selling and operating expenses before receipts₦250,000₦300,000

These assumed figures show a cash schedule, not a recommended budget. If the next order requires a ₦400,000 deposit before customers pay, the business has a ₦100,000 timing gap even if the first order will eventually be profitable. Identify that gap before committing to both orders.

Separate stock arrival from cash recovery

For a prepaid import, cash exposure can begin well before inventory reaches the business. Track days in production, transit, storage and customer credit separately. A shorter shipping route helps only if earlier arrival leads to earlier usable sales or deployment. Paying extra for air freight does not improve cash recovery when customers will not buy until the same fixed date.

Run a slower-sales scenario using your own evidence. If expected first-month receipts fall from ₦800,000 to ₦400,000, which obligations become difficult? Consider reducing the order, negotiating a legitimate staged commitment or retaining more reserve. Do not assume a new loan or supplier concession will appear when needed.

Use customer deposits carefully

If customers preorder, state the product, expected timing, cancellation terms and uncertainty clearly. Keep records of deposits and the obligations attached to them. Deposits are not free cash: you may need to deliver or refund according to the agreed terms. Avoid using money for one committed customer order to fund unrelated speculative stock.

Set a cash-based reorder rule

Review both demand and the lowest projected cash balance before reordering. Reserve amounts for unavoidable operating costs and any outstanding shipment charges. A discount for early payment should be compared with the cost of reducing that reserve. Where a purchase would leave the business unable to meet existing obligations, a smaller order or later reorder may be the stronger decision.

After each shipment, replace forecast dates and costs with actual ones. Record why the forecast differed: factory delay, clearance, slow sales, customer credit or an omitted expense. That record improves the next cash plan more than repeatedly assuming the best case.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • Nigerian import prohibition reference
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: Branded Merchandise From China: Artwork and Quality Checks
articles.blogContent:
Branded merchandise can strengthen a campaign, event or client relationship, but only if the product quality and branding are good. Poor logo placement, weak print, wrong colour, cheap finishing or late delivery can damage the brand instead of promoting it.

This guide extends How To Import Corporate Gifts From China to Nigeria and is aimed at companies, agencies, churches, schools, NGOs and teams sourcing items like bottles, bags, notebooks, apparel, tech accessories, lanyards, awards and gift sets.

Branding method affects quality

Different products require different branding methods: screen print, UV print, embroidery, engraving, embossing, heat transfer or stickers. The cheapest method may not produce the best result for the material. Ask suppliers what method they recommend and request previous work evidence.

Logo quality should be checked for size, placement, colour, sharpness and durability. If brand perception matters, sample or production proof should not be skipped.

Timeline must include approval steps

Branded merchandise requires more time than plain goods. Artwork preparation, mockup review, sample production, correction, bulk production and packaging all add steps. If the item is for an event, start from the event date and work backwards.

Use Corporate Sourcing when approval and supplier management need structure. For urgent event materials, use the event sourcing guide.

Packaging changes perceived value and freight cost

A branded item may need individual boxes, pouches, sleeves or gift packaging. Packaging improves presentation but increases cost and volume. Ask for carton dimensions after packaging is included, not before.

Use the CBM Calculator and Landed Cost Estimator before approving the final product set.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Audience, purpose and quantity defined.
  • Logo artwork, colour and placement approved.
  • Mockup and sample or proof requested before bulk production.
  • Packaging and carton dimensions checked.
  • Production and shipping timeline planned backwards from event date.
  • Approval record saved before supplier payment.

Issue one artwork pack with a revision number

Provide the approved logo files, placement dimensions, colour references and any permitted variations. Name the artwork version and the person authorised to approve it. Ask the supplier to acknowledge that version before creating a sample. A logo pasted into a chat message can be compressed or confused with an older version.

Check whether a physical colour sample is necessary. Screens and mockups do not reliably prove the final colour on fabric, plastic, metal or textured surfaces. For small text, request a proof at the actual production size. Confirm spelling, phone numbers, website addresses and QR-code destinations before approval. Test the printed QR code with ordinary phones under realistic lighting.

Approval stageWhat it establishesWhat it does not establish
Digital mockupLayout and intended placementActual colour, adhesion or surface finish
Physical decorated sampleAppearance and handling of that sampleConsistency of an entire future batch
Production inspectionResults within the agreed inspection scopeA guarantee that every uninspected unit is perfect

Choose a product people can actually use

Start with the recipient and purpose. A bulky gift can be inconvenient at a conference where attendees travel by air. A desktop accessory may suit an office campaign but have little relevance to field workers. Compare expected usefulness with delivered cost and presentation, and avoid buying a complicated kit solely because it looks impressive in a supplier photograph.

Check import eligibility for each component before committing to a gift set. Branding does not change an otherwise restricted item's status. The event-materials guide explains why common kit choices need this early review. Local production or local finishing may be the practical route for part of the set.

Inspect branding as well as the underlying product

Specify the accepted position and size of the mark, the approved colour reference and relevant durability checks. A well-printed logo on a leaking bottle is still an unacceptable gift. Record product function, decoration and packaging as separate checks so a strong result in one area does not hide a failure in another.

Agree how excess prints, rejected items and unused branded packaging will be handled. Do not assume the supplier may resell your branded rejects. Keep approval and disposal arrangements in the order terms. For the next campaign, retain the approved physical sample, final artwork and actual cost per accepted item so the team can reproduce the result without starting from screenshots.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • Nigerian import prohibition reference
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: Phone Repair Parts From China: Compatibility and Quality
articles.blogContent:
Phone repair tools and selected parts can serve a steady Nigerian market because phones constantly need servicing. But repair-related imports require compatibility, quality and supplier discipline. A wrong screen, weak battery, poor tool or incompatible component can create losses for both the repairer and the customer.

This guide supports the existing guides on importing phones safely and electronics accessories. It is best for tools, accessories and selected parts where the buyer understands the technical requirement.

Compatibility is the first filter

Phone parts and repair tools must match the model and repair use case. A screen, flex, battery, camera, tool bit or adhesive can be wrong even when the listing title looks similar. Confirm model, version, grade, quantity and warranty before payment.

Keep a compatibility file by phone model. This helps avoid reordering the wrong SKU and makes it easier to train staff or assistants who help with procurement.

Grade and defect policy matter

Parts can come in different grades. Ask whether parts are original, OEM, refurbished, copy, high-copy or aftermarket, and what the supplier means by those terms. Do not use grade language without proof.

Use supplier verification and test orders before scaling. For high-risk parts, samples or small batches are safer than bulk purchase based on photos.

Fragile parts need serious packaging

Screens, glass, delicate tools and components need protective packaging. Ask for packaging photos and carton details. Damage in transit can wipe out margin even if the supplier price is good.

Use Ship With Us after supplier handover and use the Landed Cost Estimator to price parts by SKU, not only by total shipment cost.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Model compatibility confirmed before payment.
  • Supplier specialization checked.
  • Grade, warranty and defect policy clarified.
  • Fragile parts packaging reviewed.
  • Test order used before scaling sensitive parts.
  • Landed cost and selling price calculated by SKU.

Replace vague grades with a written specification

Terms such as “original”, “OEM” and “premium copy” can mean different things to different sellers. Ask what has been manufactured, reused, refurbished or replaced, and what evidence supports a genuine-brand claim. For a display assembly, record the technology, included frame, connector version and any functionality limitations disclosed by the supplier. Do not advertise a part as genuine merely because the listing uses that word.

Maintain an internal SKU for each verified model and version. Photograph the packaging label and relevant identifiers on receipt. Similar-looking parts should remain separated in storage. A technician should be able to select the correct part from the record without guessing from a photograph on a supplier's current listing.

Agree the defect process before installation

QuestionWhy it matters
When does the claim window start?A short period beginning at China dispatch may expire during transport
What checks are permitted before a claim?Installation or removed protective films may affect the supplier's terms
What evidence is required?The technician can record the correct identifiers and symptoms
Who pays return freight?A replacement promise may be uneconomic for small batches
How is a confirmed defect resolved?Credit, replacement and refund are different outcomes

Use qualified handling and testing

Have a trained repair technician define the receiving test for each part and use appropriate equipment and handling procedures. Do not improvise battery tests or install a suspect battery to see whether it works. Confirm transport acceptance and required documentation with the carrier before buying batteries or battery-containing items. Damaged or suspect components should be isolated and handled through appropriate professional procedures.

For tools, verify the actual working dimensions and compatibility with the repair process. A poor-quality bit can damage a customer's fastener; an unsuitable heating or soldering tool can damage equipment and create safety risks. Include suitable electrical specifications, support and replacement consumables in the purchasing brief.

Calculate the cost of usable parts

If 50 parts cost ₦500,000 delivered and five cannot be used, the purchase cost per usable part is about ₦11,111. A nominal ₦10,000 unit cost therefore understates the cost of the accepted stock. This assumed example excludes labour and selling expenses. Track confirmed defects, compatibility errors and installation damage separately so the supplier is judged on evidence rather than every unsuccessful repair being labelled a factory fault.

Start with a controlled batch, review results by exact model and expand only after the specification and claim process work in practice. Preserve the records for reorders because an unchanged listing title does not guarantee an unchanged component.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • Nigerian import prohibition reference
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: A Supplier Scorecard for China Imports Into Nigeria
articles.blogContent:
A supplier scorecard helps Nigerian importers stop choosing suppliers by price alone. It creates a simple way to compare supplier strength across product fit, communication, proof, pricing, payment terms, packaging, lead time and repeat reliability. This is useful for both small importers and corporate buyers.

The scorecard does not need to be complicated. It only needs to make weak assumptions visible before payment. Use it together with China Supplier Verification Checklist and How To Compare China Supplier Quotes.

Score what matters before payment

Useful scorecard categories include supplier specialization, years or platform history, response quality, product evidence, specification accuracy, price realism, MOQ flexibility, sample support, packaging, lead time and payment clarity.

Give each category a simple score from one to five. The number is less important than the thinking. If a supplier is cheap but scores poorly on proof and communication, the risk should be visible.

Use the scorecard after delivery too

A supplier may look strong before payment and disappoint after delivery. Update the scorecard with actual performance: dispatch speed, product accuracy, defect rate, packaging quality, support after complaint and repeat order confidence.

This supports repeat supply planning. Read How Nigerian Wholesalers Can Build Repeat Supply Lines From China if you want supplier records to become a business asset.

Corporate buyers need evidence, not opinions

For companies, schools, NGOs and procurement teams, a scorecard creates accountability. It shows why one supplier was selected over another and helps finance or management understand the tradeoffs.

Use Corporate Sourcing when supplier scoring, negotiation and documentation need external support. Keep the scorecard simple enough to use repeatedly; if it becomes too complicated, buyers stop updating it and the business loses the benefit.

Practical checklist before you pay

  • Score product specialization and proof quality.
  • Score response clarity and consistency.
  • Score price only after specification is normalized.
  • Score packaging, lead time and carton data.
  • Record sample or first-order performance.
  • Review score after delivery before reordering.

Use pass/fail conditions before weighted scores

Some requirements cannot be traded against price. A supplier that cannot establish the required product identity, lawful supply route or essential safety evidence should not win because its quotation is cheap. Define these conditions first. Mark unresolved mandatory evidence as pending rather than awarding an average score and moving on.

A practical weighted example

CriterionExample weightEvidence
Specification and sample result30%Approved sample report and deviations
Comparable delivered cost20%Normalised written quotation
Delivery capability20%Agreed milestones and actual order history where available
Quality controls and traceability20%Relevant records, batch identification and inspection response
Communication and issue handling10%Clear answers and documented corrective actions

These weights are an example, not an industry certification. Change them to fit the order before scoring suppliers. For a time-critical event, delivery may deserve more weight; for a technical component, competent technical acceptance remains essential regardless of the commercial score.

On a five-point scale, scores of 4, 3, 4, 4 and 3 under those weights produce 3.7 out of 5, or 74 out of 100. Keep the underlying evidence beside the number. “Good communicator” should mean something observable, such as complete answers to the specification and prompt clarification of discrepancies, rather than friendliness alone.

Define the scoring scale

Use consistent descriptions. One might mean material requirements are unanswered; three might mean the stated requirement is supported; five might mean the requirement is strongly supported by relevant verified performance. Do not give five simply because a supplier sends a polished brochure. If evidence is missing, mark it missing and identify who will resolve it.

A new supplier may lack your own delivery history. Label the assessment provisional and distinguish claimed experience from verified records. Do not invent a performance score to fill an empty cell. A controlled first order can provide evidence for the next review.

Update after delivery and after problems are resolved

Compare actual dispatch with the agreed milestone, accepted quantity with delivered quantity, and final cost with the approved quotation. Record who caused a delay where evidence permits; a carrier delay should not automatically be attributed to factory production. Track whether corrective action solved the problem on the next batch.

Keep the scorecard version used for each purchasing decision. If the weighting changes, explain why and avoid presenting the new score as directly comparable with the old one. The purpose is a defensible supplier choice and a better next order, not an impressive number detached from the evidence.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • Nigerian import prohibition reference
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: Bags and Backpacks in Nigeria: Import Rules and Buying Checks
articles.blogContent:
Before sourcing bags or backpacks for Nigerian customers, establish whether the exact goods can lawfully be imported. This guide starts with that restriction, then explains how to evaluate bags from lawful local or other approved sources.

Confirm the legal route before requesting bag samples

Nigeria's official trade portal lists bags and suitcases under import prohibitions, with specified HS-code ranges. Do not treat a backpack, handbag or branded event bag as a routine permissible import simply because it is available on a Chinese marketplace. Obtain current classification and eligibility confirmation for the exact item from the relevant authority before paying.

A forwarding quote does not establish an exemption. Neither does a supplier's suggestion to describe the goods differently. Use an accurate description, material and intended use. Where the proposed goods are prohibited, use Nigerian production or lawful local supply. Do not attempt to solve a restriction by mislabelling the shipment. The quality checks in this guide are also useful when evaluating local manufacturers and existing local stock.

Write a specification that fits the user

For a laptop bag, measure the intended device and identify whether the compartment needs additional space for a sleeve. For a school bag, consider the intended age group and obtain appropriate safety and suitability advice. For an event tote, define the actual contents and whether the recipient needs to reuse it. “Large” or “premium” is not a measurable requirement.

SpecificationWhat to record
DimensionsExternal size and usable compartment dimensions
MaterialOuter fabric, lining, padding and any coating
ConstructionSeams, reinforcement points, strap attachment and edge finishing
ClosuresZipper or fastener specification and replacement availability
BrandingApproved artwork, size, placement and decoration method
PackingProtection against deformation, scuffing and moisture

Evaluate a representative sample

Inspect stitching around handles, straps and corners, because these points experience repeated stress. Check whether lining catches in the zipper and whether pockets fit the objects they are meant to hold. Have an appropriate professional define any load or durability testing needed for the intended use. A brief hand pull is not evidence of a safe carrying capacity.

View the sample in ordinary daylight and compare it with the agreed material and colour references. Check printing and embroidery on the actual fabric. A digital mockup cannot show puckering, thread quality or how a logo behaves on a curved pocket. Keep the approved sample and require approval before material substitutions.

Compare local quotations on accepted units

For an illustrative local order of 200 bags costing ₦800,000 delivered, ten unacceptable units would raise the purchase cost per accepted bag from ₦4,000 to about ₦4,211. Add any agreed repair, packaging and distribution costs. Ask whether the supplier will replace rejects and on what schedule. These figures demonstrate the comparison method; they are not a bag-price estimate.

For bulk distribution, label cartons by colour, size or recipient group and reconcile quantities before the distribution date. Record complaints by failure type so a future order can improve the construction. The purchasing decision should start with lawful availability and end with an accepted product that suits its user, not with the lowest overseas listing price.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • NAFDAC

articles.blogTitle: Kitchen Storage Sourcing for Nigeria: Materials and Costs
articles.blogContent:
Kitchen and home storage products can sell well because Nigerian households constantly need organization, space-saving and practical everyday items. Food containers, racks, organisers, jars, baskets, drawer systems and storage boxes can be attractive, but material quality and shipping volume must be checked.

This guide connects with our product-selection and white-label home-product guides. It is useful for mini importers, household goods retailers and brand owners who want practical products instead of random trends.

Choose products with everyday demand

Home storage products work best when they solve a clear problem: small kitchens, messy cupboards, food storage, bathroom organization, wardrobe storage or cleaning convenience. Avoid items that look clever but do not match Nigerian home habits.

Use product selection guidance before choosing. Demand should be visible before you buy heavily.

Material and food-contact safety matter

If the item touches food, ask about material, heat tolerance, smell, lid fit and whether the supplier has relevant product information. For non-food storage, durability and weight capacity may matter more.

Do not import food-contact items blindly. If a product category raises safety or regulatory concerns, check official guidance before scaling.

CBM can change the economics

Storage products can be bulky, especially boxes, racks and baskets. A cheap item may become expensive if it occupies too much space. Ask for carton dimensions and packed quantity before payment.

Use the CBM Calculator and Landed Cost Estimator before deciding quantity and shipping route.

Checklist before you pay

  • Material and food-contact exposure checked.
  • Size, colour and set quantity confirmed.
  • Packaging and carton dimensions requested.
  • Breakage or deformation risk reviewed.
  • Landed cost tested before bulk purchase.
  • Variants tracked after first sales cycle.

Identify the material and import classification first

“Kitchen storage” can describe plastic household articles, metal racks, glass containers or wooden organisers. Their requirements are not interchangeable. Check current eligibility for the exact material, construction and HS classification before paying. Public prohibition references are not fully consistent: the FCCPC reference includes plastic domestic articles, while the trade portal's displayed list differs. Obtain current clarification rather than interpreting an omission as permission.

Measure the space the product must fit

For a drawer organiser, record the drawer's internal width, depth and available height. For a rack, check the shelf or counter dimensions, door clearance and mounting arrangement. A photograph can make a product look much larger than it is. Show actual dimensions in your own listing and distinguish external container dimensions from usable internal capacity.

Ask whether the price is for one container, a complete set, lids only or a mixed-size bundle. Request a component list. If a six-piece set means three containers and three lids, describing it as six containers will create avoidable returns. Photograph the complete delivered set rather than relying on the supplier's promotional arrangement.

Match food-contact evidence to real use

Identify the material and intended contact conditions, then ask for relevant test documentation for the exact product. Have a competent adviser assess suitability and applicable requirements. Do not infer microwave, freezer, dishwasher or hot-food suitability from appearance, a recycling symbol or an unsupported marketplace claim. Avoid making those claims in your own listing until they are substantiated.

Sample observationCommercial implication
Lid opens and closes consistentlyReduces frustration and mismatched-set complaints
Parts can be cleaned as instructedHelps assess suitability for the intended household routine
Nested pieces separate without damageChecks whether compact packing creates scratches or deformation
Rack fits the intended spaceSupports accurate dimensions and customer expectations

Compare nesting savings with breakage risk

Suppose 60 sets occupy three cartons, each 60 × 40 × 50 cm. The total is 0.36 cubic metres, or 0.006 cubic metres per set. If revised packing reduces that to two identical cartons, total volume becomes 0.24 cubic metres. Confirm that the tighter pack still protects lids, corners and surfaces, then ask for a quote using the final measured packing. These are dimensional examples, not freight rates.

For glass or brittle components, ask how pieces are separated and how replacement lids or single damaged units are supplied. A set can become unsaleable when only one component breaks. Include that risk in the cost per accepted set rather than treating all delivered pieces as saleable inventory.

Use first-batch feedback to narrow the range

Track returns by reason: wrong dimensions, missing components, breakage, difficult closure or a claim the product did not meet. Correct the product or listing before reordering. Keep the strongest size combinations and discontinue variants that do not fit customers' actual spaces. A smaller, well-documented range is easier to replenish consistently than many visually appealing sets with unclear specifications.

Further references

  • Standards Organisation of Nigeria
  • NAFDAC

Percentage of eligible product cost

Buy From Chinese Websites currently pays 2% of eligible product cost. The percentage does not apply to freight, customs duties, service fees, penalties or unrelated non-product invoice lines.

If eligible products cost ₦800,000, the arithmetic starting point is ₦16,000. If the total invoice is higher because shipping and other charges were added, those excluded lines do not increase the calculation. The transaction must still be fully paid and remain eligible through review.

Fixed commission per eligible transaction

Supplier Reports, Phones and Laptops, and Supplier Verification use fixed commissions. This makes the calculation easy: the eligible completed transaction earns the configured amount in its currency, regardless of excluded add-ons.

The current rates are ₦5,000 or US$5 for Supplier Reports, ₦20,000 or US$15 for Phones and Laptops, and ₦10,000 or US$10 for Supplier Verification. The applicable currency comes from the configured transaction context; an affiliate cannot choose the more attractive conversion after the event.

Recurring subscription commission

Supplier Intelligence currently pays 10% of eligible subscription payments on a recurring basis. If a referred customer makes a qualifying ₦50,000 subscription payment, the starting calculation is ₦5,000. A later qualifying renewal can create another commission.

Recurring does not mean irrevocable or lifetime-guaranteed. Each payment must be successfully completed and satisfy the programme rules. Cancellations, failed renewals, refunds, reversals and account or attribution conditions can affect future or pending commission.

Per-unit freight commission

Ship with Us uses final eligible billed quantity. Depending on the plan, that may be US$0.50 per KG, ₦750 per KG, or ₦10,000 per CBM for an eligible Nigeria sea-volume route.

If a shipment is estimated at 100 kg but finally billed at 92 eligible kg on the ₦750 plan, the calculation begins at ₦69,000. If a sea shipment is finally billed at 1.8 eligible CBM on the ₦10,000 plan, it begins at ₦18,000. Duties, storage, verification, penalties, handling and unrelated charges remain excluded unless explicitly configured.

Why commission enters review

The current review period is 14 days. A review window lets the platform account for payment reversals, refunds, duplicated transactions, service cancellations, fraud indicators and eligibility problems. It also gives partners a clearer distinction between pending and available balances.

Do not treat pending commission as cash already owed or promise collaborators a share before it becomes available. Use the dashboard status, transaction reference and timestamps for reconciliation.

What does not earn commission

  • Clicks, impressions, copied links or account registrations by themselves.
  • Unpaid quotations, abandoned requests or rejected transactions.
  • Invoice components explicitly excluded from the commission basis.
  • Refunded, reversed, duplicated, fraudulent or self-dealing transactions that breach the terms.
  • A service that is not enabled for affiliate commission in the current dashboard configuration.

How to forecast responsibly

Forecast from a funnel, not from a fantasy income claim. Estimate qualified visitors, the proportion who create the right service request, the proportion who complete payment, the typical eligible transaction basis, and the proportion that survives review. Keep each assumption visible.

For shipping, separate KG and CBM plans. For Supplier Intelligence, separate first payments from renewals. For fixed services, count eligible completed purchases rather than total leads. This produces a model you can improve with actual dashboard data.

The practical next step

Use the rate model to select content with the best audience fit, then measure eligible paid outcomes. If the dashboard rate differs from an older article or screenshot, use the current dashboard configuration and update your promotion.

Frequently asked questions

Which Sure Imports service has recurring commission?

Supplier Intelligence currently pays 10% on eligible subscription payments, including qualifying renewals.

Does the 2% buying commission include shipping?

No. It is based on eligible product cost; shipping, duties, fees and other non-product costs are excluded.

When is shipping commission calculated?

After the linked invoice is fully paid, using the final eligible billed KG or CBM and the configured plan rate.

Can rates change?

Yes. Services, rates, currencies and eligibility rules may change. The affiliate dashboard is authoritative.

Are the examples guaranteed earnings?

No. They only illustrate the arithmetic. Actual commission requires eligible, paid and reviewed transactions.

articles.blogTitle: Sure Imports Affiliate Program: Earn From Import and Shipping Referrals
articles.blogContent:
The Sure Imports affiliate program gives creators, consultants, community operators and businesses a structured way to earn when customers they introduce complete eligible import, supplier-intelligence or shipping transactions. It is not a scheme that pays for traffic alone. It connects a useful recommendation to a real service, records the relationship, and calculates commission only when the qualifying commercial event occurs.

That distinction matters in cross-border trade. A customer may need help buying from a Chinese website today, verifying a supplier next month and shipping cargo later. The programme is designed around those practical needs, with service-specific tracking, review rules and reporting in one affiliate workspace. This guide explains the complete model as verified on 11 September 2026.

The strongest affiliates will not simply paste links everywhere. They will help an audience understand a costly or confusing decision, recommend the right Sure Imports route, and set accurate expectations about what earns commission. That approach creates trust, protects conversion quality and can turn useful education into a durable acquisition channel.

Sure Imports affiliate commission rates at a glance

Eligible serviceCommission verified 11 September 2026Commission basisReview period
Buy From Chinese Websites2%Product cost only14 days
Supplier Reports₦5,000 or US$5One eligible paid report14 days
Phones and Laptops₦20,000 or US$15One eligible completed purchase14 days
Supplier Intelligence10% recurringEligible subscription payments14 days
Supplier Verification₦10,000 or US$10One eligible paid verification14 days
Ship with UsUS$0.50/kg, ₦750/kg, or ₦10,000/CBMFinal eligible billed weight or volume14 days
LineScout Sourcing10% / 2%Eligible commitment fee / eligible product or sourcing project payment14 days

Rates, eligibility rules and currencies can change. The configuration displayed in the affiliate dashboard at the time of an eligible transaction is authoritative. Commissions are not earned for clicks, account registrations or unpaid requests.

What the Sure Imports affiliate program is

An affiliate receives trackable programme links for eligible Sure Imports services. When a referred customer follows the appropriate journey and later completes the qualifying paid transaction, the system can attribute that outcome to the affiliate. Eligible commission then enters a review period before it becomes available under the programme rules.

The programme covers more than a single product category. Its current portfolio spans assisted buying, supplier research, device procurement, recurring supplier intelligence, supplier verification, freight and LineScout sourcing. This breadth is useful because import audiences rarely have only one problem. A business owner might first need a machine, bulk product or white-label sourcing project, then shipment execution.

Joining does not make an affiliate an employee, freight carrier, customs broker, supplier, or official representative with authority to make promises on behalf of Sure Imports. Affiliates introduce customers and explain published services accurately. Sure Imports remains responsible for accepting, pricing and delivering the underlying service.

Who the programme is built for

The programme can fit import educators, YouTube and TikTok creators, newsletter publishers, bloggers, WhatsApp or Telegram community administrators, procurement consultants, business associations, software platforms and agencies whose customers already ask about China purchasing or shipping. Audience relevance matters more than raw follower count.

A niche operator with 500 business owners who trust their recommendations may create more eligible outcomes than an entertainment page with a much larger but unrelated audience. Before applying, identify the recurring questions people already bring to you: how to pay a Chinese seller, whether a supplier is genuine, how to source a production machine or white-label product, how much freight may cost, or how to move cargo to Nigeria.

  • Creators: publish demonstrations, comparisons, checklists and case-led education.
  • Consultants and agents: refer needs that fall outside their own scope without pretending to deliver the Sure Imports service.
  • Communities: place the right service link beside genuinely helpful answers and resources.
  • Businesses and platforms: use the developer workspace and API contract where programmatic shipping-request creation suits their customer journey.

The seven eligible service routes

Buy From Chinese Websites

This route is for customers who have product links from supported Chinese websites and need Sure Imports to help complete the purchase. Commission is based on the eligible product cost, not the entire invoice. Shipping, duties, handling, penalties and other non-product charges are excluded from the percentage basis.

Supplier Reports

A supplier report gives a buyer structured information for a sourcing decision. The affiliate earns the configured fixed amount when an eligible referred report is paid and survives review. A search, form start or unpaid request is not enough.

Phones and Laptops

This route serves customers buying eligible devices through Sure Imports. It uses a fixed commission per qualifying completed purchase. Affiliates should avoid advertising a specific device price unless that price appears on a current Sure Imports page, because inventory, specifications and exchange-rate conditions can change.

Supplier Intelligence

Supplier Intelligence has a recurring commission model. An affiliate can earn the configured percentage from eligible subscription payments attributed to the referred customer. Recurring does not mean guaranteed forever: each payment must qualify, and refunds, reversals, cancellations or other exclusions can affect eligibility.

Supplier Verification

This service helps customers investigate a supplier before committing more capital. It uses a fixed commission for an eligible paid verification. Factory-visit transport and other expressly excluded charges do not increase the affiliate commission.

Ship with Us

Ship with Us lets affiliates introduce customers who already have goods to move. The configured commission depends on the shipment billing unit and currency. Weight-based routes can pay per final eligible kilogram, while qualifying sea freight to Nigeria can pay per final eligible cubic metre.

LineScout Sourcing

LineScout is the Sure Imports sourcing workspace for individuals and small businesses that need machinery, bulk finished products or white-label products. Affiliates receive a dedicated LineScout referral link in the dashboard. The configured commission is 10% of an eligible commitment fee, excluding applicable fees, and 2% of the eligible product or sourcing-project payment, excluding shipping and processing fees.

Shipping remains a separate Ship with Us commission based on final eligible billed KG or CBM. Banks, large companies, institutions, government bodies, NGOs and other organisations with formal procurement requirements should use Sure Imports Corporate Sourcing, not LineScout.

How attribution works from link to commission

Attribution begins when a potential customer uses an affiliate’s tracked route or when an authorised business integration creates a shipping request under that affiliate’s API credentials. The system stores the relevant ownership data so that a later eligible transaction can be connected to the referring partner.

A tracked visit is evidence of a referral interaction, not a commission. The customer must complete the service-specific qualifying event. For shipping, an early quantity is only an estimate. Commission is calculated from the final eligible billed weight or volume after the linked invoice is fully paid, using the configured rate and currency.

API-created shipping requests have explicit affiliate ownership. That ownership is attached to the accepted request and is not silently replaced by another affiliate. Request-level ownership is separate from the customer’s general affiliate relationship, which helps businesses create requests for their customers without rewriting unrelated account history.

For LineScout, use the dedicated referral URL displayed in the affiliate dashboard. It sends the prospect into the LineScout account journey and preserves the referral relationship when validly claimed. Affiliates should copy that personalised link rather than inventing a referral parameter on a public LineScout URL.

Pending, approved, available and reversed are different states

A useful affiliate dashboard must show more than a headline balance. Sure Imports separates the operational stages so partners can understand what has been recorded, what remains under review and what can be paid. A newly generated commission normally begins in a pending or review state. The current configured review period is 14 days for the eligible services listed above.

Review protects customers, affiliates and the company when a payment is refunded, reversed, duplicated, disputed or attached to an ineligible charge. Once a commission satisfies the rules, its status can progress according to the payout workflow. Affiliates should plan cash flow around available commission, not around clicks, estimates or pending amounts.

How to promote the programme without damaging trust

Start with the user’s question, not with your link. Explain the decision, show the cost components people commonly overlook, identify who a service is suitable for, and state what information the customer should prepare. Then disclose that you may earn a commission and place the link where it naturally helps the reader act.

Good content can rank in search because it resolves a specific intent: shipping from China to Nigeria, checking a Chinese supplier, buying from 1688 or Alibaba, or importing a laptop. One accurate guide can keep attracting qualified readers long after publication. Messaging communities can also work, but repeated unsolicited posts are more likely to create complaints than customers.

LineScout creates additional high-intent topics: how to write a machine specification, how to compare production-line quotations, how to source bulk finished goods, how to choose packaging for a white-label product, and what information a sourcing brief must contain. These subjects help prospects prepare for a real project instead of sending vague enquiries.

  • Use the exact service-specific link from the affiliate dashboard.
  • Place a clear affiliate disclosure near the recommendation.
  • Do not promise guaranteed savings, delivery dates, approval or earnings.
  • Do not alter screenshots or quote obsolete commission rates as permanent.
  • Measure completed eligible outcomes, not vanity traffic alone.

A 30-day launch plan for a new affiliate

WeekPrimary jobUseful outputMetric to watch
Week 1Choose one audience problemOne service guide and one comparison postQualified visits
Week 2Build practical proofChecklist, walkthrough or frequently asked questionsStarted service journeys
Week 3Distribute with contextNewsletter, video, community answer and follow-upAttributed requests
Week 4Review and improveUpdate weak calls to action and answer objectionsEligible paid outcomes

Do not begin by covering every service. Select the route closest to your audience’s present demand. An import education channel may start with Buy From Chinese Websites or Supplier Verification. A manufacturing or private-label community may start with LineScout. A logistics platform may start with Ship with Us and the API. A device community may begin with Phones and Laptops.

After the first month, use dashboard evidence to expand. If people click but do not create requests, the content may be too broad or the call to action unclear. If requests start but rarely become eligible transactions, improve qualification and expectation setting rather than generating more low-intent traffic.

Business integrations and the shipping API

Businesses that already serve merchants can create shipping requests programmatically for their customers and earn commission on eligible completed shipments. The developer workspace provides API-key management, scopes, documentation, request reporting and exports. This is useful for commerce tools, procurement platforms, agencies and operational teams that do not want staff to re-enter the same customer and shipment information manually.

The contract includes shipping-plan discovery, idempotent request creation and request-status retrieval. An accepted API request receives a Sure Imports request identifier and locked affiliate attribution. Developers should begin inside the affiliate dashboard, protect keys as secrets and test their request mapping against the published OpenAPI document.

What the programme does not promise

No legitimate affiliate programme can promise income simply because someone creates an account. Results depend on audience fit, accurate education, demand, conversion, service eligibility, payment completion and compliance with the terms. Commission configurations can change as services, corridors and economics evolve.

Affiliates should not collect customer money on behalf of Sure Imports unless a separate written arrangement expressly authorises it. They should not present themselves as Sure Imports staff, fabricate testimonials, bid on restricted brand terms, misstate shipping costs or hide the commercial relationship. Sustainable growth comes from informed recommendations and transparent disclosure.

Useful Sure Imports resources for your audience

Readers new to the process can begin with the complete China-to-Nigeria import guide. People evaluating marketplaces can use the Alibaba buying and shipping guide. Shipping-focused audiences can compare the air-freight guide with the sea-shipping guide.

Linking to a genuinely relevant explanation before the commercial route can improve decision quality. It also prevents an affiliate link from carrying the entire burden of education.

The practical next step

Choose the one Sure Imports service that best matches a problem your audience already discusses. Create a clear account, read the terms, collect the current tracking link from the dashboard and publish one genuinely useful answer. Then use completed eligible transactions, not raw clicks, to decide what to build next.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Sure Imports affiliate program free to join?

Creating an affiliate account is free. Participation and commission eligibility remain subject to the current affiliate terms, account review and service rules.

Do I earn when someone clicks my link?

No. A click or registration alone does not earn commission. The referred customer must complete the qualifying paid event for an eligible service.

Can a business become an affiliate?

Yes. Businesses can participate and can use the developer workspace and shipping API where programmatic request creation fits their customer journey.

Is Ship with Us included?

Yes. Eligible shipments can generate commission according to the configured billing unit, route, rate and currency shown in the affiliate system.

Can I earn from LineScout sourcing?

Yes. LineScout is an eligible affiliate service for machine, bulk-product and white-label sourcing. The current configuration pays 10% of an eligible commitment fee and 2% of the eligible product or sourcing-project payment. Shipping is commissioned separately under Ship with Us.

Are Supplier Intelligence commissions recurring?

The configured model is recurring on eligible subscription payments. Each payment must qualify, and reversals, refunds or cancellations can affect commission.

Where can I see the latest rates?

Use the affiliate dashboard after signing in. The table in this article was verified on 11 September 2026, but dashboard configuration is authoritative.

Do not expose customer details or screenshots of private requests. Direct people to official Sure Imports routes for quotes, payment and support.

Consultants and sourcing professionals

Consultants may receive enquiries they cannot or do not want to fulfil directly. The affiliate programme provides a referral route, but it does not transfer responsibility for the Sure Imports service to the consultant. Explain which party is performing each task.

A shipping affiliate program in Nigeria should reward partners for introducing genuine freight demand, not merely for sending anonymous traffic. How shipping commission is calculated

Shipping often begins with an estimate, but an estimate is not the commission basis. Cargo may be reweighed or remeasured after it arrives at the warehouse. Packaging, consolidation and the carrier’s billing rules can change the final chargeable quantity. Sure Imports therefore uses the final eligible billable KG or CBM linked to the fully paid invoice.

For example, a request estimated at 80 kg that is finally billed at 74 eligible kg uses 74 kg for commission. A sea shipment billed at 2.4 eligible CBM uses that final volume. The dashboard configuration determines whether a plan is denominated in naira or US dollars.

Charges that do not automatically increase commission

The programme excludes customs duties, storage, verification, penalties, handling and unrelated invoice charges unless a future configuration expressly includes them. This prevents a partner from earning more because a customer incurred a penalty or avoidable storage cost.

Affiliates should explain freight choices without representing every invoice line as commissionable. The clean message is that commission follows the final eligible logistics quantity and the plan’s configured rate.

The referral journey

  1. Choose the Ship with Us link or approved integration route in the affiliate dashboard.
  2. Explain what information the customer needs: origin, destination, goods description, approximate weight or volume and contact details.
  3. The customer or authorised business integration creates the shipping request.
  4. Sure Imports reviews the request, confirms the applicable plan and handles the service process.
  5. After the linked invoice is fully paid, the system calculates commission from the final eligible quantity.
  6. The commission remains subject to the 14-day review period and programme rules.

Content that attracts qualified shipping leads

The most useful content answers questions that arise before a shipment request. Compare air and sea freight, explain actual versus volumetric weight, show how packaging affects volume, and clarify which product details influence handling. Sure Imports already has detailed guides to air freight from China to Nigeria and sea shipping from China to Nigeria.

A strong call to action follows the explanation: invite the reader to create a shipping request with the best available estimate and allow Sure Imports to confirm the operational details. Avoid publishing a universal transit time or rate where route, cargo type and current market conditions matter.

For agencies, platforms and business communities

Businesses can create shipping requests for their customers through the affiliate API. This is different from sending every customer to a public link. The API can place request creation inside a commerce, procurement, marketplace or customer-support workflow while preserving affiliate ownership of each accepted request.

A business should use one external reference per request, send an idempotency key and store the returned Sure Imports request identifier. Keys require the appropriate shipping scopes and should stay in a secure server environment, never in browser code or public repositories.

Compliance and expectation setting

Do not describe yourself as the carrier unless that is independently true, and do not collect freight payments while implying they are being paid directly to Sure Imports. Disclose the affiliate relationship. Use current official information for restricted goods, service availability and quotes.

Good qualification protects conversion. Ask whether the goods are already purchased, where they are located, how they are packed, the likely quantity and the destination. If the customer still needs purchasing support, direct them to the appropriate buying service instead of forcing the shipping route.

The practical next step

Build one practical shipping resource for a specific audience or cargo pattern, add a transparent disclosure, and use the Ship with Us route from your affiliate dashboard. Businesses with recurring volume can then evaluate the API for a more integrated workflow.

Does an estimated weight determine my commission?

No. Commission uses the final eligible billed KG or CBM after the linked invoice is fully paid.

Yes. A configured Nigeria sea-volume plan can pay per final eligible CBM.

Are customs duties commissionable?

Not under the current standard exclusions. Duties, storage, verification, penalties, handling and unrelated charges are excluded unless explicitly configured.

Can my company submit requests by API?

Yes. Approved affiliates can use scoped API keys in the developer workspace to create and track customer shipping requests.

articles.blogTitle: Sure Imports Shipping Affiliate API: Integration Guide for Businesses
articles.blogContent:
The Sure Imports shipping affiliate API allows an approved business affiliate to create shipping requests for its customers without sending staff through a separate manual form for every enquiry. It is designed for commerce tools, procurement platforms, agencies, communities and operational systems that already collect the basic customer and cargo information.

The integration preserves affiliate ownership at the request level. When Sure Imports accepts a request created with your API key, the response includes the attribution identifier and lock time. If the linked shipping invoice is eventually paid and remains eligible, commission is calculated using the final billable shipping quantity and the rate configuration for that plan.

API base resources

PurposeMethod and endpoint
Discover eligible shipping plansGET https://www.sureimports.com/api/v1/shipping-plans?destinationCountry=Nigeria
Create a customer shipping requestPOST https://www.sureimports.com/api/v1/shipping-requests
Retrieve a requestGET https://www.sureimports.com/api/v1/shipping-requests/REQUEST_ID
OpenAPI 3.1 contractGET https://www.sureimports.com/api/v1/openapi

Read the live OpenAPI contract during implementation rather than copying an old payload from a screenshot or article. The machine-readable contract is the source for current field constraints and response shapes.

Authentication and key safety

The API uses a Bearer API key issued in the affiliate developer workspace. Shipping creation and retrieval require the appropriate shipping:write and shipping:read scopes. A secret is displayed once and can be revoked, so store it in a server-side secret manager immediately.

Never place the key in frontend JavaScript, a mobile application bundle, analytics events, support screenshots or a public source repository. If a key may have leaked, revoke it and issue a replacement. Use separate keys where independent systems need distinct audit and rotation boundaries.

Discover a plan before creating a request

A shipping plan determines operational context including destination and billing unit. Query the plan list using the customer’s destination, present only suitable choices in your interface and store the selected shippingPlanId. Do not hard-code an identifier indefinitely because available plans can evolve.

The request quantity must be expressed in the returned plan’s unit. The current contract uses shipment.estimatedQuantity. Your interface should label that value clearly as an estimate and should not imply that it fixes the final freight charge or commission.

Create an idempotent shipping request

POST /api/v1/shipping-requests
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_API_KEY
Idempotency-Key: your-stable-request-key
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "customer": {
    "firstName": "Customer first name",
    "email": "customer@example.com",
    "phone": "+234..."
  },
  "shipment": {
    "shippingName": "Internal shipment label",
    "destinationCountry": "Nigeria",
    "shippingPlanId": "selected-plan-id",
    "estimatedQuantity": 25,
    "description": "Clear description of the goods"
  },
  "externalReference": "your-unique-reference"
}

The Idempotency-Key must contain 8 to 120 characters. Generate one stable key for the logical creation attempt and reuse it when retrying after a timeout. Do not generate a fresh key for every retry, because that defeats duplicate protection.

Use a unique external reference that maps to your own order, lead or service record. Store the request ID and status returned by Sure Imports. A successful creation returns HTTP 201 with the request identifiers, customer identifier and locked ownership details.

Attribution and commission semantics

An accepted API-created request is owned by the affiliate whose active key created it. That ownership is locked for the request. Request ownership does not overwrite the customer’s general affiliate relationship for unrelated journeys.

Request creation does not itself generate payable commission. The early estimated quantity does not set commission either. When a linked shipping invoice becomes fully paid, the system uses the final eligible billable KG or CBM and the plan’s configured commission rate and currency to create the commission snapshot.

Design for errors and retries

HTTP statusMeaning and handling
400Fix invalid fields, units, formats or missing required data before retrying.
401Check the Bearer credential; rotate it if exposure is possible.
403The key or affiliate lacks the required scope or permission.
404The plan or request resource was not found. Refresh plan data where relevant.
409Resolve an idempotency or external-reference conflict. Do not create blind duplicates.
429Respect Retry-After and back off with jitter.
500 or 503Retry safely with the same idempotency key and alert if failures persist.

Production integration checklist

  • Keep keys in a managed server-side secret store and document rotation ownership.
  • Cache plan discovery briefly, but refresh when a plan is unavailable or changes.
  • Validate required customer and shipment fields before making the API call.
  • Use one stable idempotency key and one unique external reference per logical request.
  • Log request IDs, response status and your reference without logging the API secret.
  • Handle 429 responses using Retry-After and bounded exponential backoff.
  • Reconcile request status and eligible commission through the affiliate dashboard and exports.
  • Tell customers that Sure Imports will assess and confirm the request; do not present an estimate as a final quote.

Privacy and customer communication

Submit customer data only when you have a lawful basis and have told the customer that the information will be shared with Sure Imports to handle the shipping request. Collect only the fields needed for the transaction. Protect exported reports and restrict access to operational staff.

The affiliate dashboard uses privacy-conscious reporting, including masked information where appropriate. Your own application should follow the same principle. Avoid placing full customer data in idempotency keys, external references or logs.

The practical next step

Create an affiliate account, open the developer workspace, read the live OpenAPI contract and implement plan discovery before request creation. Start with a small controlled flow, verify attribution and reconciliation, then expand the integration once error handling and customer consent are proven.

Frequently asked questions

Can the API create shipping requests for my customers?

Yes. An approved business affiliate can create requests under its API credentials and preserve request-level affiliate attribution.

Which field contains the estimated weight or volume?

Use shipment.estimatedQuantity in the unit returned by the selected shipping plan.

Why is an idempotency key required?

It lets a client safely retry a creation attempt without unintentionally producing duplicate requests.

Does HTTP 201 mean commission has been earned?

No. It means the request was accepted. Eligible commission depends on a fully paid linked invoice, final billable quantity and programme review.

Where is the API documentation?

The developer workspace links to the documentation, and the current OpenAPI 3.1 contract is available from the public API endpoint listed above.
